tools.name: browser_task
tools.description: Execute a browser automation task in a real Chrome browser running in a WebRun cloud environment (docs.webrun.ai). Creates a session, runs the task, and auto-terminates. Best for simple one-off tasks. May navigate, fill forms, and submit data on third-party websites as the task requires.

tools.name: create_session
tools.description: Create a persistent session in a real Chrome browser running in a WebRun cloud environment (docs.webrun.ai), for multi-step workflows. Returns a sessionId for subsequent commands. With an initial task the browser may act on third-party websites immediately.

tools.name: send_task
tools.description: Send a new task to an existing browser session (from create_session). The real Chrome browser may navigate, fill forms, and submit data on third-party websites as the task requires.

tools.name: pause_session_task
tools.description: Pause the task currently running in a browser session. Resume it later with resume_session_task.

tools.name: resume_session_task
tools.description: Resume a previously paused task in a browser session.

tools.name: stop_session_task
tools.description: Cancel the task currently running in a browser session, keeping the session alive for new tasks.

tools.name: terminate_session
tools.description: End a browser session and free its resources. The session and any running task cannot be resumed afterwards.

tools.name: guardrail_response
tools.description: Respond to a guardrail trigger when the browser agent needs human input (credentials, clarification, approval). The response is handed to the live agent, which continues acting on it.

tools.name: get_task_status
tools.description: Check the status of a task previously started in a browser session. Use to poll for completion or detect guardrails. Read-only: reports on the task without affecting it.

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: Capture a screenshot of the current browser page in an active session. Returns the screenshot as an inline image. Read-only.

tools.name: list_sessions
tools.description: List all active browser sessions for this account. Read-only.

tools.name: list_environments
tools.description: List available browser environments (persistent profiles) for this account. Returns environment IDs needed for persistent sessions in browser_task or create_session. Read-only.

name: get_workflow
description: Full detail of one workflow: prompt template, {{variables}} and their defaults, trigger + schedule, run settings (starting URL, timezone, model, proxy, output contract, files), memory state, and any pending logins. Identify by workflowId or exact title. Read-only; proxy credentials are masked.

labels.name: create_workflow
labels.description: Create a new saved workflow. READINESS BAR: if you could not execute the prompt yourself as a human in a browser — which site, which records, which fields, delivered where, matched to each recipient how — it is not ready; first collect the missing business facts from the user (see the TASK INTERVIEW

labels.name: update_workflow
labels.description: Update an existing workflow. Supply workflowId plus only the fields to change: prompt, trigger, schedule, run settings, variables, presentation. Object and array fields are replaced whole; pass null to clear an optional field. Renaming via title keeps the slug stable. The stored schedule stays a sav

labels.name: trigger_workflow
labels.description: Run a workflow now in its deployed environment. This is the ONLY correct way to run or TEST a saved workflow — a run started here carries the workflow's rules, tracking and memory; browser_task/create_session runs do not. When the user says "run it", "run it once", "test it" or "try it" about a work

labels.name: create_agent
labels.description: Create a scheduled agent — a recurring or one-time automation that runs on a timer in a real Chrome browser. Two modes. WORKFLOW MODE: pass workflowId plus a schedule — the platform copies everything else (prompt, starting URL, output contract, model, proxy, policy, files) from the workflow and bake

labels.name: list_agents
labels.description: List the account's scheduled agents (cron deployments): schedule, status, next/last run, and whether each is standalone or deployed from a workflow. Scoped to the bound environment when this connection has one; pass scope "all" for every environment. Read-only.

labels.name: pause_agent
labels.description: Pause an active scheduled agent — it stops firing until resumed. Get agentId from list_agents.

labels.name: resume_agent
labels.description: Resume a paused scheduled agent — recomputes its next run and reactivates it. A completed work-list agent restarts with a fresh full pass. Refuses if the agent's expiry has passed (extend it on the dashboard first).

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_workflow · Private data: guardrail_response, get_workflow, create_workflow, create_agent · Public sink: browser_task, send_task, create_workflow, trigger_workflow · Destructive: browser_task, create_session, terminate_session, list_workflows, get_workflow, create_workflow, update_workflow, trigger_workflow, create_agent, list_agents, resume_agent.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_workflow · Private data: guardrail_response, get_workflow, create_workflow, create_agent · Public sink: browser_task, send_task, create_workflow, trigger_workflow · Destructive: browser_task, create_session, terminate_session, list_workflows, get_workflow, create_workflow, update_workflow, trigger_workflow, create_agent, list_agents, resume_agent

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
